_comment: Regulatory rules engine for the DP review tool. Each rule tests a project's stated parameters and reports what the regulations require. HARD RULE: a rule may only ASSERT a requirement when `sourceTier` is `primary` and the figure was confirmed on that source. Everything else is phrased as a question for the planner to resolve — `kind: "question"` — and must never read as a legal conclusion. Adding a rule with kind:"requirement" and a non-primary tier fails validation.

fields.label: Stated IT load
fields.help: The load the application states, not the site's ultimate build-out.

fields.label: Municipality
fields.help: Drives the land use rules pulled from the municipal matrix.

fields.label: On-site generation
fields.help: Generation proposed on the site, including backup.

fields.label: Nearest sensitive receptor
fields.help: Distance to the closest dwelling, school or care facility.

rules.title: Meets the large data centre threshold
rules.detail: At 75 MW or more the project is a large data centre for the purposes of Alberta's data centre framework, which is the trigger for the province's grid connection process rather than an ordinary load connection.
rules.ask: Confirm the stated load is the connection load and not just first-phase IT load. Ask what the ultimate build-out is.

rules.title: Below the 75 MW large data centre threshold
rules.detail: The stated load sits under the threshold that triggers the province's large-load process.
rules.ask: Check whether phasing or a later expansion would cross 75 MW. A staged application that ends above the threshold should be assessed as though it were there from the start.

rules.title: AESO's interim connection capacity is reported fully allocated
rules.detail: AESO's interim approach set a 1,200 MW cap on large-load connections through 2028, and it is reported as fully allocated. A project without a secured connection cannot assume grid capacity exists.
rules.ask: Ask for the AESO queue position and correspondence. Without it, the timeline in the application is unsupported.
rules.sourceName: AESO — Interim approach to large load connections

rules.title: Bridged connections are time-limited
rules.detail: Bridging allows limited early connection under strict reliability conditions, including an obligation to curtail when the grid requires it, and it does not run indefinitely.
rules.ask: Confirm what happens to the operation when bridging ends. A condition tying occupancy to a firm connection may be appropriate.

rules.title: On-site generation proposed
rules.detail: Generation on the site is regulated separately from the data centre building itself, and by a different body than the municipality.
rules.ask: Has an application been made to the Alberta Utilities Commission? A municipal development permit does not authorise the generating facility, and approving one without the other can leave a half-permitted site.

rules.title: AI data centre levy is part of the fiscal picture
rules.detail: Alberta legislated a levy on AI data centres. It does not change the planning test, but it is relevant to any claim the applicant makes about net municipal benefit. This entry cites a law firm summary rather than the Act, so treat the detail as orientation and check the legislation itself.
rules.ask: If the application argues fiscal benefit, check whether it accounts for the levy and for the province's position that costs are not to be transferred to ratepayers or municipal taxpayers.

rules.title: Evaporative cooling consumes water rather than circulating it
rules.detail: Open-loop and hybrid cooling lose water to evaporation, so consumption is not recovered downstream. This is the single biggest driver of a data centre's water footprint.
rules.ask: What is the consumptive volume, at design load and at peak summer temperature? A figure quoted as an annual average understates the summer draw that actually stresses a supply.

rules.title: Non-municipal water needs its own authorisation
rules.detail: Drawing groundwater or surface water is licensed provincially and separately from the development permit.
rules.ask: Is there a licence or a transfer in hand, and does its volume match the application's stated use? A permit granted against an unlicensed supply is not deliverable.

rules.title: Municipal supply — check headroom, not just connection
rules.detail: A connection being physically possible is not the same as the system having capacity for the load through its design horizon.
rules.ask: Has utilities confirmed available capacity at design load, and what does it displace? Ask for the assessment in writing.

rules.title: Sensitive receptor within 1 km
rules.detail: Data centre noise is continuous and tonal rather than intermittent, so it is experienced differently from most industrial noise at the same measured level.
rules.ask: Is there an acoustic assessment at the receptor, modelled at full load with cooling running, and does it address low-frequency content and night-time levels rather than an averaged daily figure?

rules.title: Large site — check the plan hierarchy, not just the district
rules.detail: A site of this size often engages an area structure plan or a municipal development plan policy that sits above the land use bylaw.
rules.ask: Does the proposal conform to the applicable statutory plan, and is an amendment being sought alongside the permit?

municipalRules._comment: Evaluated against municipalities.json rather than hardcoded, so the matrix stays the single source of truth. A blank cell renders as 'needs research', never as a pass.

useClassDiscretionary.title: Use is discretionary here
useClassDiscretionary.detail: A discretionary use materially widens the grounds on which the application can be refused or conditioned, compared with a permitted use.
useClassDiscretionary.ask: Confirm the current bylaw text — several Alberta municipalities changed this classification during 2026.

useClassPermitted.title: Use is permitted here
useClassPermitted.detail: Where the use is permitted and the application meets the bylaw's standards, the grounds for refusal are narrow, and conditions must attach to matters the bylaw actually regulates.
useClassPermitted.ask: Focus scrutiny on the standards you can enforce — servicing, setbacks, noise, and cost recovery — rather than on the principle of the use.

unknown.title: Municipal position not yet verified
unknown.detail: This municipality's row in the matrix has not been confirmed against its current bylaw.
unknown.ask: Read the bylaw directly before relying on any assumption about use class. Do not infer it from a neighbouring municipality.
